data.title: Core/HTTP: card delete (DELETE /v1/cards/:id + tombstone event + idempotency)

fields.description:
Add a first-class card-delete path so junk/test/superseded cards can be hard-removed instead of being closed-as-done with a comment (the current workaround used during the 2026-07 board cleanup, which hit exactly this gap).

Scope:
- DELETE /v1/cards/:id HTTP route (mirror existing PATCH auth/actor/idempotency: X-Work-Cards-Actor header, Idempotency-Key, optimistic version in ?version= query param).
- CLI: `cards delete <id> --version N` (serverless + HTTP, like patch/claim).
- MCP: a `delete_card` tool (the MCP tool list currently has no delete either).
- Core: Service.RemoveCard(id, version, actor) — atomic. Emit a new `card_removed` durable event (typed constructor in internal/core/events.go per EVENTS.md §4 no-raw-literals rule) carrying the removed card's id/type/title snapshot in Diff for replay/audit. Persist via the existing commitCard seam (or the ClaimAtomic-style atomic path if no card row update is needed — decide and document).
- Safety: delete is a hard, irreversible mutation. Require the current version (optimistic concurrency) so a stale client cannot delete a card that changed underneath it. Consider a workspace setting to soft-delete (tombstone) vs hard-delete; default to hard-delete + event to match append-only audit design. Refusing to delete a card that still has inbound links is an open question — propose: reject with 409 if any inbound links exist (caller removes links first), OR cascade-remove the card's links but refuse to cascade across cards. Pick one and document in SPEC.md §11.
- Docs: SPEC.md §11 (add the route), §8 (add card_removed to the event catalog + diff shape), INTEGRATOR-REFERENCE.md §2/§4, MCP.md (tool table), DEVELOPER-REFERENCE.md §9 (CLI). Status: [proposed].

Out of scope: bulk delete, undo/recycle, retention windows.

Acceptance:
- `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` green with new tests covering: delete by current version succeeds and emits card_removed; stale version returns 409 version_conflict; delete is idempotent under a replayed Idempotency-Key (returns the original 204/200); deleting a card with inbound links behaves per the chosen policy with a test.
- OpenAPI spec (internal/openapi) updated; `cards delete` works in both serverless and HTTP modes; MCP `delete_card` tool listed and working.

data.title: Events seam 3d: deadline min-heap scheduler for temporal conditions (status_timeout, card_idle)

fields.description: docs/EVENTS.md §11.2; design already refined in INTEGRATION.md comments (deadline min-heap, no fixed tick, sleeps until earliest deadline, empty heap = no wakeups). This is the hardest and riskiest piece of the condition-event system — land it as its own isolated slice, after the instant-condition machinery (3a-3c) has already validated Signal/Emit/persist:true. Deadlines armed from a denormalized status_since column + a fired-marker keyed by (card,status,status_since); reconstructible from state, nothing persisted for scheduling itself. Lazy/refcounted: only scheduled while a monitor has a live consumer (SSE filter, hook/webhook, or persist:true), dropped when the last consumer disconnects. Acceptance: unit-testable scheduler with an injected clock (no real sleeps in tests); zero-wakeup idle test (empty heap does not spin); refcount test (deadline dropped when last consumer disconnects, re-armed on reconnect); crossing-state idempotency test.

data.title: Core/CLI: serverless CLI — auto-select backend (direct core+sqlite vs HTTP)

fields.description:
Let read/write CLI commands work without a running HTTP server, in addition to (not instead of) the server.

Already partly true: the transport-agnostic core (internal/core) is shared by all surfaces, and export/import/mcp already skip HTTP — they call sqlite.Open + core.NewService directly against the workspace DB. Extending list/get/create/patch/... to do the same is mostly wiring.

Why: zero-config one-shots (`cards list` in a .cards/ dir just works, matching the new git-style workspace resolution); lower latency; no port/URL bookkeeping.

Two catches that mean HTTP cannot simply be dropped: (1) the event bus is in-process — a CLI writing directly to the DB bypasses a running server bus, so SSE live updates and status_changed hooks would not fire; (2) SQLite is single-writer across processes — direct writes while `cards serve` holds the DB risk SQLITE_BUSY/lock contention (WAL allows concurrent readers).

Clean design (matches ARCHITECTURE notes): CLI auto-selects its backend — if CARDS_URL is set or a server is detected, use HTTP so events/hooks/SSE stay correct; otherwise open core+sqlite directly for a fast serverless one-shot. Cost: a small backend interface the CLI commands target, with HTTP and direct-service implementations behind it.

data.title: Events: condition events + monitors (WIP, time-in-status, empty lane, idle)

fields.description: Declarative board 'monitors' -> condition events on the bus. Instant (eval synchronously after the triggering mutation): wip_exceeded/cleared, lane_drained/refilled, card_blocked/unblocked. Temporal (status_timeout, card_idle): emitted by a monitor-evaluator goroutine beside the hook supervisor, driven by a deadline min-heap (sleeps until the earliest deadline, NO fixed tick; empty heap = no wakeups). Deadlines armed from a denormalized status_since column + a fired-marker keyed by (card,status,status_since); reconstructible from state, nothing persisted. Lazy/refcounted: deadlines scheduled only while a monitor has a live consumer (SSE filter, hook/webhook, or persist:true), dropped when the last consumer disconnects. Idempotent crossing-state tracking; core emits only, never acts. See docs/INTEGRATION.md.
